name: News Corporation

profile.description: News Corporation is a global media and information services company operating Dow Jones (The Wall Street Journal, Barron's, Factiva, Dow Jones Risk & Compliance and Dow Jones Energy), Digital Real Estate Services (a majority stake in Australia's REA Group and Realtor.com operator Move), Book Publishing (HarperCollins) and News Media (The Times, The Sun, The Australian, New York Post). Fiscal 2026 (ended June 30) revenue rose 6.8% to a record $9.03B with net income of $573M [2][3]. Fiscal Q4 2026 revenue rose 11% to $2.34B, total segment EBITDA jumped 31% to $423M, and net income from continuing operations rose 167% to $230M, led by REA (+21%) and Dow Jones (+7%, EBITDA margin 28.1%) [3][4].

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): News Corp has steadily rebuilt itself from a newspaper publisher into a portfolio weighted toward digital real estate and B2B information — Dow Jones Risk & Compliance and Dow Jones Energy now sit beside the WSJ, and Digital Real Estate Services revenue grew 19% to $553M in fiscal Q4 2026 with segment EBITDA up 46% [3][4]. AI Deployment (2/2): The May 2024 multi-year global licensing agreement with OpenAI, valued by the WSJ at more than $250M over five years in cash and technology credits, is shipping AI revenue today and grants access to OpenAI tools for internal products [5][6]. Market Share (2/2): REA Group is the dominant Australian property portal (revenue +21% in Q4) and the WSJ is the leading US business news franchise, with Dow Jones digital advertising up 10% [3][4]. Product Pipeline (1/2): Management guides to continued Dow Jones revenue strength, improved Dow Jones Energy B2B growth and further margin expansion in fiscal 2027 [4], but without named product launches. R&D Intensity (0/1): No reported R&D line [2].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): News Corp describes itself as creating and distributing authoritative and engaging content and information services; it is clear about what it does, and CEO Robert Thomson has made the defence of journalism's economic value a public cause [5], but it is not distinctive beyond the media industry. Community Impact (1/2): Standard corporate philanthropy and ratings agencies score ESG management as strong (Sustainalytics ranks it 13th of 266 media companies) [8], but institutional investors have alleged 'rampant nepotism' and 'failed corporate governance' tied to the UK phone-hacking legacy [7]. Employee Retention (0/2): No retention or tenure data found. Insider Buying (0/2): No meaningful net insider buying identified; control rests with the Murdoch family via dual-class shares.

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as a Growth stock (dividend yield 0.69% is below the 2% Dividend threshold). D/E of 31.6% is well inside the 70% target (1.0) and quarterly revenue growth of 10.8% YoY clears 10% (1.0) [1]. ROE of 8.0% scores 0.53 (2x weight) and profit margin of 6.3% scores 0.32 [1]. The 5-year revenue CAGR is -0.7% on an as-reported basis (FY2021 $9.36B to FY2026 $9.03B), depressed because FY2021 included Foxtel, which has since been sold — on a continuing-operations basis revenue grew ~4.1% a year from FY2023 [2]; the as-reported figure scores 0.29 (2x weight). Forward P/E of 19.3 is just inside the 20x target (1.0), but Forward PEG of 2.61 scores only 0.20 (2x weight) [1]. Weighted sum 5.34/10, rounded to 5. Liquidity is ample: 3.92M avg volume × $29.12 = ~$114M daily.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (4/9): Generative AI answer engines directly threaten the traffic and advertising economics of News Media and parts of Dow Jones; publishers argue AI models trained on their content have created chatbots that 'now compete with them as sources of information' [5][6]. The defences are real but partial: subscription paywalls, proprietary B2B datasets (Factiva, Risk & Compliance, Dow Jones Energy pricing) and REA's two-sided property marketplace are much harder to substitute, and Thomson has chosen to 'woo rather than sue' to get paid for content [5]. AI Opportunity (1/1): The OpenAI licensing deal, valued at more than $250M over five years, is quantifiable AI-derived revenue [6].

infinite_game.summary: Sinek would see a company with an enduring franchise but a finite posture. News Corp's portfolio moves — selling Foxtel, building B2B data and digital real estate — have been shrewd, and Robert Thomson has led since 2013, yet the company's public language is about fighting Google, AI companies and rivals for value, its governance remains family-controlled and litigated, and its cause is defined more by what it opposes than by a future it is building.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): The aspiration to provide authoritative journalism and information has substance, and Thomson's campaign that quality content must be paid for is consistent [5]. But the stated purpose is largely descriptive, and the phone-hacking legacy and nepotism allegations [7] undercut the claim that the cause shapes behaviour.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Leadership is stable — Thomson has been CEO since the 2013 separation and Dow Jones and REA have experienced management teams. No evidence of exceptional psychological safety was found, and the dual-class Murdoch control structure has drawn governance lawsuits [7].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): News Corp's competitive framing is combative — Thomson describes the OpenAI deal as a chance to 'recalibrate the world of search' long dominated by Google [5], and the company is known for litigating against AI companies it considers free-riders. Rivals are adversaries, not teachers.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): The shift from a print-heavy newspaper group to one where digital real estate and B2B information drive growth is meaningful [3][4], and the Foxtel sale removed a declining pay-TV asset [2]. The changes came through acquisitions and divestitures layered on the legacy model rather than a single cause-driven reinvention.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Thomson took an early and public stand that AI companies must pay for journalism, signing the first major global licensing deal with OpenAI rather than accepting uncompensated scraping [5][6], and the company sold Foxtel to focus on higher-growth digital assets. Capital allocation is otherwise conventional, including ongoing buybacks.

investment_thesis: News Corp has turned into a collection of high-quality digital and information assets wrapped in a media holding company: fiscal 2026 revenue reached a record $9.03B, net income rose 23% to $573M [2], and fiscal Q4 accelerated with revenue +11%, total segment EBITDA +31% and Digital Real Estate EBITDA +46% [3][4]. REA Group's dominance in Australian property search, Dow Jones' 28.1% EBITDA margin, and a balance sheet with only 31.6% debt-to-equity [1][4] give the company options, while the $250M+ OpenAI deal shows its content can be monetised in the AI era [6]. Management guides to further margin expansion in fiscal 2027 [4].
thesis_continued: The bear case is valuation and structure. At 28x trailing and a 2.61 PEG, the stock prices in growth that its 8.0% ROE and 6.3% net margin do not yet support [1], and as-reported revenue is below FY2021 levels after the Foxtel sale [2]. AI search could erode traffic to the WSJ, The Times and New York Post faster than licensing deals replace it [5], HarperCollins faces generative-content pressure, Realtor.com remains a distant number two in US property search, and Murdoch dual-class control plus governance litigation [7] limit the value minority holders can unlock from the REA stake.
key_catalysts: Fiscal 2027 margin expansion at Dow Jones as digital advertising (+10% in Q4) and B2B Energy/Risk & Compliance growth outpace print declines [3][4]
Continued double-digit REA Group growth from price increases and rising Australian residential listings [3]
Additional AI content licensing agreements following the $250M+ OpenAI deal, adding high-margin revenue [6]
key_risks: AI answer engines reducing referral traffic and ad revenue for WSJ, The Times, The Sun and New York Post faster than licensing replaces it [5]
Australian housing slowdown hitting REA listings volumes, the largest single EBITDA driver [3]
Dual-class Murdoch family control and governance litigation alleging nepotism limiting minority shareholder value [7]
